summary:
Euro area industrial producer prices rose 1.6 per cent month on month in July 2026, while EU prices increased 1.4 per cent.
Energy drove the monthly rise, with prices up 5.6 per cent in the euro area and 4.7 per cent in the EU.
For textile and apparel sourcing teams, the data flags upstream cost pressure across European manufacturing inputs and pricing talks.

title: UK businesses flag rising supply-chain risks from conflict, shipping
summary:
In August 2026, UK businesses reported elevated supply-chain concerns, with 28 per cent worried about international conflict and 21 per cent about shipping disruptions. 
Concern over climate-related risks rose to 13 per cent. 
Among affected firms, 53 per cent expected higher sourcing costs and 46 per cent higher transport costs, while energy and fuel price concerns remained high.

title: Australia GDP rises 0.4% in Q2 2026 as cautious households curb demand
summary:
Australia’s GDP rose 0.4 per cent in the June quarter and 2.1 per cent through the year, indicating subdued demand conditions for suppliers and retailers.
Household consumption grew 0.4 per cent, with cautious spending, fuel price pressure and travel disruption shaping demand.
Goods imports rose 2.4 per cent and exports 0.8 per cent; net trade added 0.1 percentage points to growth.

title: Global FDI rises 6% as UNCTAD flags concentrated recovery
summary:
Global FDI rose 6 per cent to $1.6 trillion in 2025, but developing economies grew 2 per cent; top 20 hosts drew over 80 per cent.
AI infrastructure, semiconductors, critical minerals and energy-transition technologies took 44 per cent of greenfield value.
Developing sourcing bases need energy, skills, facilitation and supplier links to turn FDI into capacity, jobs and technology transfer.

title: Vietnam attracts FDI worth $40.63 bn in Jan-Aug 2026
summary:
Vietnam attracted $40.63 billion in registered FDI in the first eight months this year, up by 55.4 per cent YoY. 
The processing and manufacturing sector received the largest FDI share, attracting 55.9 per cent of the total newly-registered capital. 
Vietnamese investment abroad, including newly-registered and additional capital, reached $2.62 billion, 4.7 times higher than a year earlier.

title: Thailand, China re-polyester DTY, POY prices turning higher?
summary:

Thailand recycled filament yarn export offers broke a five-week standstill in late August, with DTY 100D/48F up 12 per cent in a week and POY 150D up 3 per cent.
Firmer feedstock costs, easing bale collection and autumn restocking supported higher offers.

title: China calls on France to stop anti-ultra-fast-fashion law
summary:
China’s commerce ministry says France’s anti-ultra-fast-fashion law may breach World Trade Organization non-discrimination rules.
It says the measure targets Chinese-invested cross-border e-commerce platforms and distorts fair competition.
Exporters, platforms and sourcing teams face uncertainty if France proceeds and Beijing takes necessary measures.

title: PVH beats profit estimates despite 3% sales decline in Q2
summary:

summary:

US-bound shipments faced combined 50 per cent reciprocal tariffs from August 27, 2025 to February 6, 2026, before duties were reversed.
ICRA projected a 6 to 9 per cent FY2026 revenue decline; TexPro showed Q1 2026 apparel exports to the US down nearly 26 per cent.

title: South India cotton yarn turns soft amid falling cotton prices
summary:

Gujarat cotton retreated as a sharp fall in ICE cotton futures dampened demand.

title: RMG exports from B’desh in green zone as shipment jumps in August 2026
summary:

Knitwear grew 6.17 per cent to $4.193 billion, while woven apparel increased 3.81 per cent to $3.301 billion. 
Home textile exports gained 11.17 per cent to $154.55 million, but cotton and cotton products fell 13.02 per cent to $82.24 million.

title: As Sri Lanka’s exports grow, is apparel losing momentum?
summary:

Apparel and textiles fell 6.50 per cent to $2.88 billion, diverging from broader export growth. 
July apparel and textile exports dropped 8.8 per cent to $437.59 million, with shipments declining across the United States, European Union and United Kingdom.

title: A meeting that highlights the fraying edges of Bangladesh’s RMG story
summary:
BGMEA told the President that nearly 400 garment factories have closed in Bangladesh over three years, as production costs rose almost 40 per cent. 
Inadequate gas supplies, higher energy tariffs, wages and bank interest rates are forcing many factories to operate below half capacity. 
Garment exports contracted 1.64 per cent in FY2025-26 and fell 1.92 per cent in July of FY2026-27.

Textiles, garments and other manufactured textile articles made up 45.28 per cent of Sri Lanka’s industrial exports in the period.
